gaps.sentence: Need we ___ the whole report, or just the summary?
gaps.hint: modal need takes the bare infinitive
gaps.explanation: When 'need' is a modal in questions and negatives, it takes the bare infinitive: read.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: In this lab, food and drink ___ be brought past the reception area.
gaps.explanation: Written prohibitions use 'must not': must not be brought.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to be at the airport three hours before long-haul flights.
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' shows obligation from outside the speaker: have to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: Where is Anna? I am not sure — she ___ be in the library.
gaps.hint: an uncertain possibility, not really sure
gaps.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility the speaker is unsure about: might be.
